rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He attaches the promise of divine aid either to the implied statement that the places were not demolished because God repelled some people by others, or to the earlier permission to fight.
rows.anchor: عطف عليه أو على قوله { أذن } قوله : { ولينصرون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming God instead of using a pronoun universalizes the rule and ties it to the quality of whoever supports Him, from among Muslims or others.
rows.anchor: وأظهر ولم يضمر تعميما وتعليقا للحكم بالوصف فقال : { من ينصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God arranges support through ordinary causes or extraordinary breaches of custom, as in early Muslim conquests and miraculous crossings and victories.
rows.anchor: بما يهيىء له من الأسباب , إجراء له على الأمر المعتاد , وبغير أسباب خرقا للعادةن كما وقع في كثير من الفتوحاتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is powerful over whatever He wills and cannot be overcome; whoever has Him as helper is victorious, while that person's enemy is subdued, even if the supported party is weak.
rows.anchor: ثم علل نصره وإن ضعف المنصور , بقوله : { إن الله } أي الذي لا كفوء له { لقوي * } أي على ما يريد { عزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description shows that the empowered people fight for God rather than for themselves, after being described as wrongfully driven from their homes.
rows.anchor: وصفهم بما يبين أن قتالهم له , لا لهم , بعد أن وصفهم بأنهم أوذوا بالإخراج من الديار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the pillar of religion and signals watchfulness over God and turning away from pursuit of transient things.
rows.anchor: أقموا الصلاة } اي الني هي عماد الدين , الدالة على المراقبة والإعراض عن تحصيل الفاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving alms signals detachment from accumulated wealth and awareness that it is provision for the journey onward.
rows.anchor: وآتوا الزكاة } المؤذنة بالزهذ في الحاصل منه , لالمؤذن بعمل النفس للرحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recognized good is what sacred law recognizes and permits.
rows.anchor: وأمروا بالمعروف } وهو ما عرفه الشرع وأجاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He associates forbidding wrong with having intimacy only with God, fearing only Him, and placing hope in Him.
rows.anchor: ونهوا عن المنكر } المعرف بأنه لا أنس لهم إلا به سبحانه , ولا خوف لهم إلا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse demonstrates the legitimacy of the caliphate of the four imams.
rows.anchor: والآية دالة على صحة خلافة الأئمة الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Empowerment is certain in the end, while God conceals the beginning so Satan may have a share in it and the sincere can be distinguished from the false and wavering.
rows.anchor: ذكره للعاقبة وطيه للبادئة منبه على أنه تعالى يجعل للشيطان - كما هو المشاهد في الأغلب - حظا في البادئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final outcome belongs wholly to God and reaches the resurrection, when no one acts independently and no one speaks without special permission.
rows.anchor: وأما العاقبة فهي متمحضة له إلى أن يكون آخرذلك القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denial need not distress the Prophet: God has destroyed earlier peoples who were powerful, and can seize the present rejecters as well.
rows.anchor: { وإن يكذبوك } اي أخذتهم وإن كانوا أمكن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine ending in the verb belittles the deniers in relation to God's power, despite their being among the strongest people.
rows.anchor: وأتى سبحانه بتاء التأنيث تحقيرا للمكذبين في قدرته وإن كانوا أشد الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He omits a preposition before the earlier peoples because their great age makes them seem to have occupied all of time; he then lists them in chronological order.
rows.anchor: كأنهم قد استغرقوا الزمان كلهن لم يأت بالجار فقال : { قبلهم قوم نوح }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence names Noah's people, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Abraham's people, Lot's people, and Midian's people, with brief contextual characterizations of each.
rows.anchor: ساقهم على حسب ترتبيهم في الوجود فقال : { وعاد } اي ذوو الأبدان الشداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax changes for Moses because he brought unmatched visible and audible signs; the Egyptians collectively denied him, while only a few of his own people did so, making the example especially consoling.
rows.anchor: غير سبحانه الأسلوب تنبيها على ذلك , وعلى أن الذين أطبقوا على تكذيبه القبط , وأما قومه فما كذبه منهم إلا ناس يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's delay followed by seizure both consoles the Prophet and warns current deniers; the particle ثم emphasizes the length of their respite.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن طول الإملاء بأداة التراخي لزيادة التأسية فقال : { ثم أخذتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakir means God's repudiation of their deeds in the form of punishment; the rhetorical question warns these deniers to fear the same.
rows.anchor: فكيف كان نكير * } أي إنكاري لأفعالهم , فليحذر هؤلاء الذين أتيتهم بأعظم ما أتى به رسول قومه مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding evidence from 2:106 establishes that disputing God's ruling is unbelief; this verse follows without a conjunction because the connection is complete.
rows.anchor: فعلم أن منازعتهم فيه كفر , فلذلك أتبع هذا قوله من غير عاطف لما بينهما من تمام الاتصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For every community in every age God prescribed a rite or law through which they gather around their Creator in obedience, or gather around their own desires when it opposes His command.
rows.anchor: لكل أمة } أي في كل زمان { جعلنا } أي بما لنا من العظمة { منسكا } أي شرعا لاجتماعهم به على خالقهم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says the basic Arabic meaning of mansak is a place a person regularly visits, for good or ill.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن جرير أم أصل المنسك في كلام العرب هو الموضع الذي يعتاده الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will perform the prescribed rite; God defends them against its opponents until the matter is established, whether for their felicity or misery.
rows.anchor: هم ناسكوه } أي متعبدون به , لأنا ندافع عنهم من يعاديهم فيه حتى يستقيم لهم أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubting God's ability to establish the rite is unbelief; obeying it brings faith and gain, while opposing it brings unbelief and loss.
rows.anchor: فمن شك في قدرتنا على تمكينهم منه فهو كفور , فإن وافق الأمر كان ربحا وإيمانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not heed disputes raised through satanic doubts about his religion, including objections that abrogation would imply a change of knowledge or badāʾ in God.
rows.anchor: بما يلقيه الشيطان إليهم من الشبه ليجادلوا به , من طعنهم في دينك بالنسخ بقولهم : لو كان من عند الله لما أمر اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that abrogation implies badāʾ: it instead shows God's foreknowledge of outcomes and complete power to legislate.
rows.anchor: فليس الأمر كما زعموا , بل هو دال على العم بالعواقب والاقتدار التام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is reported to have been revealed after pagans, including Budayl b. Waraqāʾ and Bishr b. Sufyān al-Khuzāʿī, argued over slaughter: Muslims ate animals they killed but not those killed by God, meaning carrion.
rows.anchor: وروي أنها نزلت بسبب جدال الكفار بديل بن ورقاء وبشر بن سفيان الخزاعين وغيرهما في الذبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is to call all people to his Lord and carry out each command without fear or calculation of consequences; arranging the eventual success of the religion belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وكان التعبير بما تقدم من تحويله إليهم لتأكيد الأمر مع دلالته على إجلاله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is firmly on straight guidance because it comes from the All-Knowing, Almighty, even if its course appears to change.
rows.anchor: فإنه تأصيل العليم القدير وإن طرقه التغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking sexual gratification beyond the permitted bounds includes adultery, sodomy, masturbation, and sex with animals.
rows.anchor: فمن ابتغى } أي تطلب متعديا { وراء ذلك } العظيم المنفعة الذي وقع استثناؤه بزنى أو لواط أو استمناء يد أو بهيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such people transgress because these acts cause confused lineages, violated honor, wasted wealth, and conflict among people.
rows.anchor: أي المبالغون في تعدي الحدود , لما يورث ذلك من اختلاط الأنساب , وانتهاك الأعراض , وإتلاف الأموال

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi includes sexual integrity, duties to God such as prayer and fasting, inward qualities such as sincerity and truthfulness, and human trusts such as deposits and goods among the trusts to be kept.
rows.anchor: أو في المعاني الباطنة كالإخلاص والصدق , أو بينهم وبين خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A covenant is the greatest trust, so it is singled out after the general mention of trusts; keeping it means fulfilling, preserving, and repairing it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان العهد أعظم أمانة , تلاها به تنبيها على عظمة فقال : { وعهدهم راعون * } أي الحافظون بالقيام والرعاية والإصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the most excellent and binding religious trust; believers carefully preserve its obligations and sunnas and strive for its perfection.
rows.anchor: لا يتركون شيئا من مفروضاتها ولا مسنوناتها , ويجتهدون في كمالاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the word in the singular to indicate prayer as a genus; the other readers use the plural to signal its numbers and kinds.
rows.anchor: وحدت في قراءة حمزة والكسائي للجنس , وجمعت عند الجماعة إشارة إلى أعدادها وأنواعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening and closing this list of virtues with prayer magnifies its importance.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في افتتاح هذه الأوصاف واختامها بالصلاة من التعظيم لها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that prayer is the best of deeds; the author gives no grading.
rows.anchor: أن خير أعمالكم الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The virtuous are true heirs, inheriting God's abode through nearness to Him and ultimately inheriting worldly land after contending against more numerous and powerful disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي المستحقون لهذا الوصف المشعر ببقائهم بعد أعدائهم فيرثون دار الله لقربهم منه واختصاصهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to Hajj 22:5 is enough to establish the connection between Sūrat al-Muʾminūn and the preceding sūra.
rows.anchor: [ الحج : 5 ] وهذا كاف في التحام السورتين

words: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِن سُلَٰلَةٍۢ مِّن طِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning Paradise, the sūra proves resurrection through the first creation, moves to the greater created cosmos, then warns through earlier peoples, turns to gratitude for human distinction, and returns to proofs of resurrection and divine oneness.
rows.anchor: استدل على القدرة عليه بابتداء الخلق للإنسان , ثم لما هو أكبر منه من الأكوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative begins with Noah because he was the first prophet and his ark rescue recalls that humanity descends from him; after warnings and blessings, the next sūra continues the preceding discussion of guarding sexual integrity.
rows.anchor: وابتدأ بقصة نوح عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنه أول , ولأن نجاته كانت في الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulāla is a small amount extracted gently, like a clipping or a bit of dust; it refers to Adam's clay, drawn from the earth's clay in a balanced form and thus proves God's power to recreate.
rows.anchor: من شيء قليل , بما تدل عليه الصيغة كالقلامة والقمامة , انتزعناه واستخلصناه برفق

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā reports from the Prophet that Adam was created from a handful taken from all the earth, so his descendants vary in color and in good and bad dispositions; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إن الله خلق آدم عن قبضة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines creation as measuring out components that will appear as a form after mixture and composition; Biqāʿī applies this to clay's mixture and the unexpected emergence of a human.
rows.anchor: لأن الخلق - كما مر عن الحرالي في أول البقرة : تقدير أمشاج ما يراد إظهاره بعد الامتزاج والتركيب صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is the second, purer origin of humanity and the source of living things; jaʿala describes bringing about a result through a cause, while thumma marks the striking transition from clay to water.
rows.anchor: أتبعه سبحانه أصله الثاني الذي هو أطهر الطهورين : الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the clay itself or to the human kind extracted from clay and developed through its successive individuals.
rows.anchor: هذا النوع المسلول من المخلوق من الطين بتطوير أفراده ببديع الصنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drop is a flowing fluid with no trace of clay remaining.
rows.anchor: نطفة } أي ماء دافقا لا أثر للطين فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarār is originally a verbal noun used as the name of a place; the secure receptacle comprises the loins and ribs, then the womb, and is protected from corrupting influences.
rows.anchor: في قرار } أي من الصلب والترائب ثم الرحم , مصدر جعل اسما للموضع { مكين * } أي مانع من الأشياء المفسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first transformation is extraordinary and the drop may either spoil or begin developing, so the author uses creation and thumma to mark delay and elevated rank.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تصيير الماء دما أمرا بالغا خارجا عن التسبيب , وكانت النطفة التي هي مبدأ الآدمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drop is very white; the ʿalaqa is thick, coagulated, intensely red blood.
rows.anchor: النطفة } أي البيضاء جدا { علقة } حمراء دما عبيطا شديد الحمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the clot onward, each ascending stage follows its predecessor without delay by God's unique decree, not through a process available to others; fa marks this succession.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ما بعد العلقة من الأطوار المتصاعدة مسببا كل واحد منه عما قبله بتقدير العزيز العليم الذي اختص به من غير تراخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mudgha is a small piece of flesh without shape or pattern.
rows.anchor: مضغة } أي قطعة لحم صغيرة لا شكل فيها ولا تخطيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God refines and hardens the flesh through heat and subtle processes to form bones of the head, feet, and everything between.
rows.anchor: بتصفيتها وتصلبيها بما سببنا لها من الحرارة والأمور اللطيفة الغامضة { عظاما } من رأس ورجلين وما بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clothes the bones with flesh, covering, strengthening, and binding them with ligaments and nerves.
rows.anchor: فسترنا تلك العظام وقويناها وشددناها بالروابط والأعصاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final creation refers to forming the human and breathing in the spirit, producing a living, speaking, articulate person far removed from clay.
rows.anchor: { ثم أنشأناه } أي هذا المحدث عنه بعظمتنا { خلقا آخر

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the root letters nūn-shīn-hamza indicate the elevation and loftiness of something.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : وأصل النون والشين والهمزة يدل على ارتفاع شيء وسموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is permanently established in every perfection and free of every defect; any incapacity would contradict that complete perfection.
rows.anchor: ثبت ثباتا لم يثبته شيء , بأن حاز جميع صفات الكمال , وتنزه عن كل شائبة نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proper name Allah gathers all the beautiful names and their meanings.
rows.anchor: فعبر بالاسم العلم الجامع لجميع الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāliqīn here means those who measure or determine; God best determines this wondrous creation and guides it through every human life stage.
rows.anchor: أي المقدرين , أي قدر هذا الخلق العجيب هذا التقدير , ثم طوره في أطواره ما بين طفل رضيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human development ranges from infancy through adolescence, vigorous youth, adulthood, and old age, with innumerable states known only to God.
rows.anchor: ما بين طفل رضيع , ومحتلم شديد , وشاب نشيط , وكهل عظيم , وشيخ هرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphatic mortality after extraordinary life recalls that death is a fixed condition of every contingent being, whose own nature is nonexistence, though familiarity makes death seem ordinary.
rows.anchor: وكان عتو الإنسان على خالقه وتمرده ومخالفته لأمره نسيانا لهذا المألوف كالإنكار له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse specifies the great resurrection, the basis of reward and punishment; affirming it entails affirming lesser postmortem life, and its lighter emphasis does not deny life in the grave or its questioning.
rows.anchor: وليس في ذكر هذا نفي للحياة في القبر عند السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address describes people who have committed themselves to this religion.
rows.anchor: أيألزموا أنفسهم هذا الدين { لا تدخلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the prohibition applies to each individual, it addresses the group because believers should restrain one another and prevent an individual from being overcome by Satan.
rows.anchor: فمن خان منهم منعه إخوانه , فلم يتكمن منه شيطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other people's houses are houses in which the addressees do not reside.
rows.anchor: بيوتا غير بيوتكم } أي التي هي سكنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking familiarity means asking permission so the occupants can feel at ease and the visitors can know them; answering only I does not identify the visitor, who should give a known name.
rows.anchor: أي تطلبوا بالاستئذان أن يأنس بكم من فيها وتأنسوا به , فلو قيل له : من ؟ فقال : أنا لم يحصل الاستئناس لعدم معرفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visitors should greet the residents, even temporary occupants, ask to enter, and knock if they may not hear the request.
rows.anchor: فتقولوا : السلام عليكم ! أأدخل ؟ أو تطرقوا الباب إن كان قد لا يسمع الاستئذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission and greeting are better than entering unannounced or using pre-Islamic greetings: they spare visitors from seeing what they dislike, with greater benefit in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لأنكم إذا دخلتم بغير إذن ربما رأيتم ما يسوءكم , وإذا استأذنتم لم تدخلوا على ما تكرهون

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī reports that if a person greets three times and receives no answer, the person should return, provided the host is thought to have heard; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقد روى أبو موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه : إذا سلم ثلاثا فلم يجبه أحد فليرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The etiquette invites people to remember that they dislike others exposing their private circumstances, so they should treat others as they wish to be treated; recompense matches deeds.
rows.anchor: فيعرف أن ما يسوءه غيره منه , فيفعل ما يحب أن يفعل معه خوفا من المقابلة , لأن الجزاء من جنس العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Practices required outside one's home are recommended at home too: make a throat-clearing or raise the voice in remembrance, following the warning against surprise night visits that might expose unwelcome sights.
rows.anchor: وكل ما يجب عليه في غير بيته يستحب له في بيته بنحو النحنحة ورفع الصوت بالذكر ونحوه على ما أشار إليه حديث النهي عن الطروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a house has no resident present, God's protection of privacy requires visitors not to enter.
rows.anchor: أي البيوت التي ليس بها سكناكم { أحدا } قد يمنعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering another's house is an exercise of control over another's property or rights and is unlawful without permission from its resident or another person with legal authority.
rows.anchor: لأن الدخول تصرف في ملك الغير أو حقه فلا يحل بدونه إذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visitors should leave when told to return, without taking offense: people have private matters they do not want others to see, and the truth must be followed.
rows.anchor: ولا تستنكفوا من أن توجهو بما تكرهون من صريح المنع , فإن الحق أحق أن يتبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning is purer because it avoids the humiliation of waiting at another's door and makes the host feel grateful or embarrassed at the visitor's compliance; God rewards obedience.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه طهارة من غضاضة الوقوف على باب الغير , ونماء بما يلحق صاحب البيت من الاستحياء عند امتثال أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows even deeds whose nature is hidden or ambiguous to the most perceptive people, so visitors should avoid doubtful conduct.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى عليه شيء منه وإن دق , فإياكم ومشتبهات الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While waiting for permission, stand to the right or left of the door rather than facing it, and do not look through windows, since permission protects the residents' sight and privacy.
rows.anchor: فإذا وقفتم للاستئذان فلا تقفوا تجاه الباب , ولكن على يمينه أو يساره , لأن الاستئذان إنما جعل من أجل البصر

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet's saying that when someone speaks and turns away, the conversation is a trust; the author cites Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Tirmidhī without grading it.
rows.anchor: مثل قوله صلى الله عليه السلام : ( إذا حدث الرجل فالتفت فهي أمانة ) وراه أحمد وأبو داود والترميذي عن جابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pagans mock the Prophet even though his truthful speech and noble conduct would make him an unlikely target even without a miracle, and he has also brought signs that overwhelm reason.
rows.anchor: مع ما يعلمون من صدق حديثك وكرم أفعالك لو لم تأتهم بمعجزة , فكيف وقد أتيتهم بما بهر العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun conveys their extreme mockery despite the Prophet's being far removed from ridicule.
rows.anchor: عبر بالمصدر إشارة إلى مبالغتهم في الاستهزاء مع شدة بعده صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They phrase the sneer as a question and apparent acknowledgment that God sent him, though they are in profound denial; the feigned admission intensifies their ridicule.
rows.anchor: فإخراجهم الكلام في معرض التسليم والإقرار - وهم في غاية الجحود - بالغ الذروة من الاستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In their next statement, inna is the lightened particle rather than a negation, as shown by the lām in the following verb.
rows.anchor: وعرف بأن ( إن ) مخففة لا نافية باللام فقال : { ليضلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say the Prophet nearly turns them from their gods through extraordinary signs and persistent counsel; they claim only solidarity kept them attached to idols.
rows.anchor: ليضلنا } أي بما يأتي به من هذه الخوارق التي لا يقدر غيره على مثلها , واجتهاده في إظهار النصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By claiming their steadfastness kept them with their idols, they imply the idols protect them; God threatens that they will learn the truth when punishment comes, even after a long respite.
rows.anchor: ولما لزم قولهم هذا أن الأصنام تغني عنهم , نفاه مهددا مؤكدا التهديد لفظاعة فعلهم بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they see punishment in this world or the next, they will know who was further astray: themselves or the Messenger they accused of leading them away; then deeds cannot help.
rows.anchor: حين يرون العذاب } أي في الدنيا والآخرة { من أضل سبيلا * } هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God comforts the Prophet, who grieves because he earnestly wants his people to return to what benefits them and avoid harm.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك مما يحزنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لشدة حرصه على رجوعهم , ولزوم ما ينفعهم واجتناب ما يضرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reduce god to desire and serve only passion, without a rational basis for idol-worship that could make them leave it; only God can turn such desires aside.
rows.anchor: فهم لا يعبدون إلا الهوى , وهو ميل الشهوة ورمي النفس إلى الشيء , لا شبهة لهم أصلا في عبادة الأصنام يرجعون عنها
